findings.title: Queued-entries and failed-drain branches of stream_close() have no test
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits on the old _outgoing_queue_ready and, via then_wrapped, closes the write buffer even when that future is exceptional, but the only new test empties the queue before stream_close() runs and never injects a failed entry, so a regression that closes the buffer before queued entries drain, or skips the close on a failed drain, would pass the suite.

findings.title: Server's unguarded while(source().get()) loop could see stream_closed instead of eof on…
findings.claim: Adversarial-codex claimed the server handler's unguarded drain loop can observe stream_closed rather than eof when the client closes its stream half, but tracing the eof-marker send order, the sequential process() loop, and the queue's abort/consume ordering against head 69da8f5b showed the marker is always pushed and consumed before EOS can arrive, and the identical pattern has existed unflagged since 2018 in test_stream_simple.

findings.title: Hook index in new test claimed to depend on negotiation order
findings.claim: A candidate finding argued that BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) and hooks.back() are fragile relative to negotiation order, but this was discarded because the parent connection is always negotiated before make_stream_sink creates the stream connection, making hooks.back() deterministic.

findings.title: Regression test's try/catch can pass or hang instead of failing on a regression
findings.claim: test_stream_send_after_stream_close's try/catch silently accepts a successful send; without the fix the only failure signal is put_after_close after 10 yield()s, so the test could pass or hang rather than fail explicitly on a regression, and should instead assert BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(..., rpc::closed_error).

findings.title: No test for peer disconnect racing the new drain wait in stream_close()
findings.claim: There is no test covering the peer dropping the connection while stream_close() is waiting on the old _outgoing_queue_ready, i.e. stop_send_loop() running concurrently with the new drain wait.

findings.title: New test only covers the compressor's send_empty_frame hook, not other send() callers
findings.claim: The regression test exercises only the compressor's send_empty_frame hook during the closing window and does not test other callers of send().

findings.title: queue_drained wait in stream_close() has no timeout
findings.claim: The new queue_drained wait added in stream_close() has no timeout and could in principle hang on a stalled peer, but tracing showed the pre-change write_buf.close() flush blocked on the same stalled-peer condition, so no new wedge was introduced, and the wait is unblocked by stop_send_loop()'s shutdown_output() on socket error or receive-loop exit.

findings.title: Out-of-tree compressors calling send_empty_frame during the new closing window were not…
findings.claim: Out-of-tree compressors (e.g. a dictionary-announcement hook) that call send_empty_frame and do not expect closed_error while connection::error() is still false were not audited; only the in-tree lz4 and multi_algo factories were checked.

findings.title: Unresolved _negotiated during stream_close() argued impossible but not tested
findings.claim: A stream connection whose _negotiated is still unresolved when stream_close() runs was argued to be impossible by reasoning about client/server negotiation ordering, but this invariant is not covered by any test.

findings.title: Behavior of output_stream::write on an already-closed stream was not traced
findings.claim: The behaviour of output_stream::write on an already-closed stream (whether it buffers the put, hangs, or throws) was not traced, which bears on how the new test actually fails without the fix.

findings.title: Author's claim that the new test fails without the fix commit is unverified
findings.claim: The author's verification that rpc_test passes in the debug build on 1 and 2 shards, and that the new test fails without commit f545c28a, could not be verified by this review because no build directory exists in this checkout.
